record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.context_brief: Spectrally bounded maps on II_1 factors
record.original_question: For a von Neumann factor of type II_1, does the finite-matrix characterization of unital surjective spectrally bounded linear maps remain valid? The finite-matrix statement is: a linear map T : M_n(C) -> M_n(C) is unital, surjective, and spectrally bounded, meaning r(Tx) <= M r(x) for some M >= 0 and all x, if and only if there are a Jordan automorphism S of M_n(C) and a nonzero complex number gamma such that T x = gamma Sx + (1 - gamma) tau(x), where tau is the normalized center-valued trace.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a von Neumann factor of type $\mathrm{II}_1$, with unique normalized faithful normal tracial state $\tau$ (the center-valued trace, which on a factor takes scalar values). For $x\in M$ let $r(x)$ denote its spectral radius. A linear map $T: M\to M$ is called spectrally bounded if there exists $M_0\ge 0$ such that $r(Tx)\le M_0\, r(x)$ for all $x\in M$, and unital if $T(1)=1$.

The finite-dimensional model is the following theorem on $M_n(\mathbb{C})$: a linear map $T:M_n(\mathbb{C})\to M_n(\mathbb{C})$ is unital, surjective and spectrally bounded if and only if there exist a Jordan automorphism $S$ of $M_n(\mathbb{C})$ and a nonzero complex number $\gamma$ such that
$$T(x) = \gamma\, S(x) + (1-\gamma)\,\tau(x)\,1 \qquad \text{for all } x\in M_n(\mathbb{C}),$$
where $\tau$ is the normalized trace.

Question: Does this characterization extend to every type $\mathrm{II}_1$ factor $M$? That is, is every unital surjective spectrally bounded linear map $T:M\to M$ of the form $T(x)=\gamma S(x)+(1-\gamma)\tau(x)\,1$ for some Jordan automorphism $S$ of $M$ and some nonzero $\gamma\in\mathbb{C}$?
artifact.category_tag: Spectrally bounded maps on von Neumann algebras
artifact.status_search_result: Existing results (Mathieu and collaborators) treat spectrally bounded unital surjections from properly infinite von Neumann algebras, showing they are Jordan homomorphisms; the type II_1 factor case is explicitly highlighted as an open problem, and recent literature on spectrally bounded/additive maps does not resolve it. No source confirming a solution was found.

status_evidence.title: Spectrally bounded operators from von Neumann algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Every spectrally bounded unital operator from a properly infinite von Neumann algebra onto a semisimple Banach algebra is a Jordan homomorphism.
status_evidence.claim: Known results cover the properly infinite case; the type II_1 case is not addressed there.

status_evidence.title: Spectrally additive group homomorphisms on Banach algebras
status_evidence.snippet: Results on spectrally additive maps and Jordan isomorphisms under socle/prime hypotheses.
status_evidence.claim: Recent work does not establish the type II_1 factor characterization.
